behavior_in_task_description.explanation: The instruction asks for no damage during the liftoff shown in the video, at that pad and 'at any other equivalent spot of the same station', and says nothing else about the ships or stations should change. The tests match this: no contact at rest or while climbing on all 6 Cydonia bays, plus guards that the hull mesh and pad collision stay intact. The ship and station are left for the agent to identify from the video, which is the point of this multimodal task. Shallow code workarounds would fail the geometry tests, and the 'nothing else should change' constraint and the 'damage before it visibly hits anything' clue reasonably point to the real geometry/clearance defect.

behavior_in_tests.explanation: The tests cover the resting docked pose and a 2 cm-step climb up to 10 m on every bay of the station, which covers 'at the spot shown or any equivalent spot'. The P2P tests cover 'nothing else should change': the collision mesh keeps its shape and the pads still register docking-surface contact.

informative_test_structure.explanation: TestCollisionMesh.cpp has a detailed header comment explaining the replay method. Helpers are well named (InitHeadlessEngine, ShipOnBay, LiftoffScene). Each TEST_CASE has a descriptive name and comments, and INFO messages report per-bay results.

anti_cheating_measures.explanation: The bug patches are deleted in the same RUN step that applies them. Git history is wiped and re-initialized so the fix commit is unreachable, and file timestamps are normalized. Only recording.mp4 is copied into the image, not the descriptive manifest. The agent has no network. test.sh restores src/test and the test paths from harbor_base before applying the hidden tests. The P2P guards block gutting the meshes or collision geometry.

structured_data_schema.explanation: No structured output is expected; the task is to fix model/collision data.

pinned_dependencies.explanation: Only apt packages from Ubuntu 22.04 are used, and the repository is checked out at a pinned commit hash. No pip or other unpinned language packages are installed.

typos.explanation: No typos in paths, test names, or commands. The test names in config.json, task.toml and test.patch match exactly, and file paths match the repository layout. Leftover template comments in test.sh (mentioning wx) are cosmetic and do not affect behavior.

tests_or_solution_in_image.explanation: The Dockerfile copies only bugs/ (deleted right after use) and assets/recording.mp4. tests/ and solution/ are never copied into the image.

test_deps_in_image.explanation: The image installs only the build toolchain and libraries needed to build and run Pioneer, which the agent also needs. Pre-building the unittest target is a build cache, not a test-only dependency. Hidden test sources are applied only at verification time.

hardcoded_solution.explanation: solve.sh applies the upstream developer fix patch, which edits the three .dae files: it raises the hull's lowest vertex, corrects the low-LOD landing tag, and restores pad 1's collision height. This is the standard oracle for a bug-fix task, not an echoed answer.

file_reference_mentioned.explanation: The agent does not have to produce any named output file. The tests check engine behavior through hidden test sources that the verifier adds itself.
